sentences.text:
1  India to issue a Writ of Mandamus directing the 2nd respondent to p  appropriate orders on the claim/representation dated 26.12.2022 mad  the petitioner under Section 3G(5) of the National Highways Act by  reconsidering Award dated 16.8.2022 passed by the Special District  Revenue Officer - Land Acquisition, National Highways - 844 (Hosur   Royakottai - Dharmapuri Section) and re- fix the compensation as pe  provision of Schedule I and II and Section 26(1) a and b of the Cen  Act 30 of 2013 and enhance the compensation in respect of acquired   measuring 1050 sq.mtrs. comprised in S.No.99/7, New S.No.99/7B  covered in patta No.1344 and land measuring 219 sq.mtrs comprised i  S.No.99/1A1, New S.No.99/1A2 covered in patta No.125, Echanahalli  Village, Denkanikottai Taluk, Krishnagiri District and grant adequa  opportunity to the petitioner by furnishing copies of last three ye  statistics in respect of the locality and revenue village in which   petitioner's land is situated obtained from the Registration Depart  and allowing the petitioner to peruse all records and filing writte  submissions and re-fix the compensation as per the provision of Sch  I and II and Sections 26 to 30 of the Central Act 30 of 2013 within  time frame to be fixed by this Court and also following the procedu  contemplated under Sections 18 to 27 of the Arbitration and Concili  Act.
 For Petitioner : Mr.R.Ramesh Raja  For Respondent-1 : Ms.R.Durga Rani  2/5 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis  
 For Respondents 2 & 3 : Mr.V.Veluchamy,
 Additional Government Pl  For Respondent-4 : Mr.Su.Srinivasan  ORDER
With the consent of both the parties, this Writ Petition is taken up for final disposal at the admission stage itself.

2. The petitioner has filed this writ petition seeking a direction to the second respondent to pass appropriate orders on the claim petition dated 26.12.2022 filed under Section 3G(5) of the National Highways Act by reconsidering the award dated 16.8.2022 passed by the third respondent.

3. It is needless to point out that whenever a representation of this nature is made to a Statutory Authority, there is a duty cast upon him to consider the same on its own merits and pass appropriate orders in one way or other, instead of keeping the same pending indefinitely.

As such,
non-consideration of the representation by the Statutory Authority would amount to dereliction of duty and hence, this Court will be justified in https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis invoking its Muniraj vs The Secretary To Government on 13 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83476585/
2 extraordinary powers under Article 226 of Constitution of India and direct him to consider the same within a stipulated time.

sentences.text: 4. In the light of the above observations, there shall be a direction to the second respondent herein to consider the petitioner's claim petition dated 26.12.2022, on its own merits and pass appropriate orders in accordance with law, after giving due opportunity to the petitioner as well as all other persons who may be interested in the subject property, within a period of three months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.

It is made clear that this Court has not expressed any of its views with regard to the merits of the claim of the petitioner and that it is open to the concerned respondent to consider the same on its own merits.
5. With the above direction, the Writ Petition stands disposed of.
